newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: Lithuanian seimas approves bank privatisation law.
newsitem.headline: Lithuanian seimas approves bank privatisation law.

text.p: Lithuania's seimas, or parliament, on Thursday night passed a key law to privatise two of the country's state-run banks, the parliament's press office said.

A spokeswoman for parliament told Reuters that 48 deputies supported the law, 31 opposed it, and five abstained, paving the way for the sell off of the State Commercial Bank and the Agricultural Bank.
Delivering the banks from state hands is part of the privatisation drive launched by the country's new right-of-centre government.
The previous government last year rushed to save the State Commercial bank with a fresh injection of 165 million litas in share capital after it emerged that it faced a severe liquidity crisis.
The Agricultural Bank is in better shape, with a net profit of over 25.5 million litas last year.
But the bank also faces problems stemming from soft loans to the country's struggling agricultural sector.
A number of foreign and local banks have expressed interest in buying stakes in both banks.
The law, which was put to an open vote, allows the government to privatise the banks through bids open to both foreign and Lithuanian banks and financial institutions.
The bids will be organised by the Finance Ministry.
